newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks roar on Dow Coattails.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks roar on Dow Coattails.

text.p: Mexican stocks notched up sharp gains to close near an all-time high on Monday after an all-time record on Wall Street lured foreign investors.
The leading IPC share index ended up 56.71 points, or 1.46 percent, at 3,930.09. The Dow Jones industrial average meanwhile soared 123.22 points to close at a record 7,292.75.
Dealers said the bourse had been in a lull since the IPC set its closing record of 3,938.69 points on Feb. 25.
Hector Jimenez, an analyst at the Inverlat brokerage said telecommunications stock Telmex lead the rally, which was also driven by foreign buyers.
"Foreigners were a little more active, some stocks had lagged far behind the market and Telmex also had an impact after its ADR broke resistance at 42-1/2," he said.

Telmex ADRs closed up 1-5/8 at 43-3/4 on Wall Street, while their L shares climbed 54 centavos (7 cents) to a record close in peso terms of 17.34 ($2.19). Dealers said Telmex ADRs were still substantially below 1994 levels, however, when they had traded at more than $70.
Dealers said foreign buying raised trading volume to a brisk 98.9 million shares.
"The market is waking up at last, but could could slow down once it rises above 3,960 points," a dealer said.
On the broad market, of 115 stocks traded, and gainers outpaced sliders by 62 to 30.

Tourist company Situr headed the percentage gainers' list, up six centavos (less than 1 cent) to 42 centavos (5 cents), followed by its debt-ridden holding company Sidek, which gained five centavos (less than 1 cent) to 53 centavos (7 cent s). Situr announced during the session that one of its subsidiaries had extended maturity on its medium-term promissory notes.
